canon.summary:
I researched Nevarro's canon on Wookieepedia: the articles Nevarro, Nevarro City, Nevarro Imperial base, Nevarro Mandalorian covert, Nevarro sewer, Charon River, Lava fields, Nevarro school, Office of the Magistrate, bazaar, Statue of IG-11, Clan Mudhorn homestead, The Tribe's camp and Landing yard. Their wikitext is saved in lab/nevarro/text/. No repo files were edited and nothing was committed.

I made 11 contact sheets with scripts/galaxy-refs.mjs. Article pages carry few exterior shots, so I also built 6 sheets from all 227 files in Wookieepedia's "Category:Images of Nevarro" (comic covers and merchandise removed). Those 6 came from a scratch script, lab/nevarro/catsheet.mjs, using the same tile format; each list.json also holds the file's wiki description and source episode. I downloaded about 55 key stills at 1600 px to lab/nevarro/full/ (scratch fetcher lab/nevarro/fetchfull.mjs), looked at each one, and measured the palette from them (lab/nevarro/palette.mjs).

Corrections to the brief:
- **No ziggurat:** nothing on Nevarro matches.
- **The school was not an Imperial outpost.** It was the old cantina, the Crossroads Common House, which the Client used as his office after Chapter 3. Karga turned it into the school in S2, and Gorian Shard's pirates turned it back into a cantina in S3.
- **The Imperial presence in town in S1** was the "Imperial Remnant safe house" (the Client's facility). Only its interiors are shown.

Design sources (from the wiki's behind-the-scenes notes):
- The terrain is based on the lava flows of Kailua-Kona, Hawaii.
- The stone streets and arches come from Pompeii, and the markets from Morocco and the Middle East.
- The base's outside is modelled on Eadu from Rogue One.
- Doug Chiang designed the lava tunnels like lungs: two tunnels lead down into the sewers and one leads out toward the light.

The most useful finding is in File:NevarroModel.jpg, Image Engine's untextured digital model of the S1 city, seen from above. The streets are trenches cut down into a flat lava-rock plain. Buildings line the trench walls, their roofs sit level with the rock surface, and low ribbed domes poke up at roof level. That is why the town shows only as domes on black rock from outside.

In S3 the city grows out across black lava tongues: cylindrical cream and white towers with domed caps, cobbled streets, trees and orange banners. It sits in front of a single conical volcano.

Clean, whole-building exteriors are rare. These are good inputs for an image-to-3D lift:
- the gate arch: NevarroCitySpaceport, NevarroCity-TMCh12, Landing Yard MandoS3
- the domes: NevarroCity-TMCh12, DisneyGalleryTechnology
- the Imperial base: NevarroImperialBase, which is the only exterior shot of it
- the S3 white tower: Showdown on Nevarro
- the homestead cabin: Grogu-Mando-Home-CH24
- the IG-11 statue: only a small 375x671 image

The cantina and school, the safe house, the magistrate's office and the forge are shown only from inside. No clean outside view exists in the wiki images.

landmarks.name: Nevarro City gate arch
landmarks.description: The archway into the city, with ships landing just outside it (wiki: 'An area designated for starships to land was located outside of the archway that led into the city'). S1: a tall, weathered stone arch with a round-topped opening and a ragged top, like a Pompeii ruin. S2: a post-and-lintel stone gate with an overhanging cap and a round emblem hanging from the lintel, colourful market awnings visible through it. S3: refinished, smooth pale pillars under a rounded beam-like cap with a sphere hanging below it, at the edge of a paved landing yard. In S1 a second pair of massive square pillars stands inside the city across a main street, under a concrete bridge.

landmarks.name: S1/S2 town fabric: domed stone and plaster buildings sunk into the lava rock
landmarks.description: Thick-walled grey plaster and stone blocks with sloped, stained walls. They have round-headed, recessed doorways, round porthole windows and wall lanterns, with cables strung across the streets and tan, orange or red cloth awnings. Low ribbed or banded domes sit on the roofs. The streets are trenches cut down into a flat black lava plateau, so from outside the town reads as clusters of domes, small towers and antennas on ridges of black rock (see NevarroModel). Inside is an open dirt square where Gideon's TIE landed. Best single-dome silhouettes: the left edge of NevarroCity-TMCh12 and the dome beside the arch in DisneyGalleryTechnology and NevarroCitySpaceport.

landmarks.name: Cantina (Crossroads Common House), later the Nevarro school
landmarks.era: S1 cantina; S1 the Client's office; S2 school; S3 pirate cantina
landmarks.description: The guild cantina where Karga handed out bounties. Inside: a low arched hall with a big round window, booths and dim light. After Chapter 3 the Client used it as his office. The heroes were trapped there in Chapter 8 and escaped through the sewers. Karga turned it into a school in S2: arched plaster vaults, rows of desks and the teacher droid CB-3DU. In S3 Shard's pirates made it a cantina again. It fronts the market square, and the IG-11 statue stands near its entrance. No clean whole-building exterior exists. Vane and crew.png shows its entrance steps from the street.

landmarks.name: Imperial Remnant safe house (the Client's facility)
landmarks.description: Gideon's remnant was stationed here in the city with the Client and Dr. Pershing. Din met the Client here and stormed it to rescue Grogu in Chapter 3. Interiors only: dark rooms with slatted windows. A night aerial shot shows the Razor Crest over the town during the escape. This is the only canon 'Imperial building in town'. There is no ziggurat.

landmarks.name: S3 Nevarro City (High Magistrate Karga's rebuilt boomtown)
landmarks.description: A construction-boom trade port on the Hydian Way. It has cylindrical towers of several storeys with vertically panelled or fluted walls and domed or ringed caps, some with orange-banded tops. Streets are pale cobbles between white and cream plaster facades with awnings, scaffolding and orange and yellow banners. Planted trees with pale trunks (fig or ficus-like) and potted plants line the streets, and Kowakian monkey-lizards live in the trees. Seen from the air, the city spreads over lobes of black lava with the pale landing yard on the flat ash beside it. Karga's holomap names the East Court, Pol Kushin, the shipping terminals and the trade district. Best tower silhouette: the white tower in mid-frame in Showdown on Nevarro.

landmarks.name: Office of the Magistrate of Nevarro
landmarks.description: Karga's office, where the Mythrol also worked. Inside it is a round room with a big curved window, plaster walls and a central holotable. Interior only.

landmarks.name: Statue of IG-11
landmarks.description: A life-size IG-11 standing on a rough black rock plinth, one arm raised with a blaster. It stands in the marketplace near the school entrance, in front of a pale stepped plaster wall, and is partly built from the droid's real scorched remains. In S3 Din takes the head and torso down. The only image is small (375x671), but the whole figure is visible.

landmarks.name: Landing yard / spaceport apron
landmarks.description: Ships park on open ground just outside the arch. In S1 and S2 this is packed black gravel and ash with small marker blocks (the Razor Crest, X-wings). In S3 it is a wide paved apron of pale grey slabs, with ships, droids and crowds, and the volcano behind.

landmarks.name: Nevarro bazaar (market)
landmarks.description: Near the city entrance. Stalls under sagging tan, orange and red cloth awnings on poles, set against stained plaster walls with lanterns. A Kowakian monkey-lizard roasted on a grill here in S1.

landmarks.name: Sewer, Mandalorian covert and the Armorer's forge
landmarks.description: The Tribe's hidden enclave in the sewers under the city, reached from the cantina. It has dim stone vaulted halls. The forge is a domed chamber with a raised circular hearth platform in the centre, a hanging conical metal hood above it, rows of blue gas-flame jets, warm lamp light and racks of tools. A descending tunnel leads to the underground lava river. Interior only.

landmarks.name: Charon River (underground lava river) and its tunnel mouth
landmarks.description: The lava river runs from the city's sewer out to the lava flats. The tunnel is a long, ribbed, vaulted stone tube with lava running along both edges and dark crusted lava with glowing specks between. The heroes rode a keelboat poled by the MA-13 ferry droid. The tunnel ends in a round rough-rock portal that opens onto pale lava flats with low hills beyond, where a stormtrooper platoon waited and IG-11 sacrificed himself. Wiki quote (the Armorer): 'It flows downstream toward the lava flats.'

landmarks.name: Lava fields / lava flats
landmarks.description: A wide, nearly flat plain of black ropy lava (pahoehoe) split by winding cracks and channels of glowing orange lava. Steam rises from scattered vents, and low rounded dark hills sit 1-3 km off under a blue dusk sky. Lava meerkats and qartuums live here. The 'western lava flats' later bound the land Karga gave the Mandalorians.

landmarks.name: Razor Crest landing hills (S1 Ch7 meeting and night camp)
landmarks.description: Where Din landed to meet Karga: a flat black ash and rock plain under an overcast steel-blue sky. The horizon is low and broken by flat-topped buttes and rocky crags. They camped overnight on the riverbank and rode blurrgs into town; the sunset is golden over black ridges.

landmarks.name: Nevarro Imperial base
landmarks.description: Built during the Imperial expansion into the side of a cliff overlooking a canyon, with a coolant system that let it sit among the lava. It is a long, low, multi-level slab of cold blue-grey armour hugging the cliff lip. Rows of large ribbed cylindrical tanks are stacked along its face, gun turrets and a radar dish sit on top, and a landing pad with yellow markings juts out over the drop. TIE fighters are parked on the flat plateau above. The Trexler marauder escaped through a narrow slot canyon with near-vertical dark rock walls. The outside is modelled on the Eadu lab from Rogue One; the inside is a standard Imperial hangar and corridors.

landmarks.name: Clan Mudhorn homestead (Din and Grogu's cabin)
landmarks.description: A cabin just outside the city that Karga gave Din. It is a grey rounded plaster block with a large round-cornered doorway, an oval window, wall lamps, a small dome on the roof, a porch and a hitching post. A pond lies in front, with mossy black rocks and grass tufts around it.

landmarks.name: The Tribe's camp
landmarks.description: A cluster of tents on a pale ash flat in a shallow basin ringed by low dark lava ridges. It lies between the western lava flats and Bulloch Canyon, on the land Karga gave the Mandalorians.

landmarks.name: Nevarro from orbit
landmarks.description: A blue-grey and white cloud-swirled globe over dark land, with red lava specks on the night side.

canon.landscape:
Canon terrain is 'ashen, rocky, volcanic': black sands, rocky flats and hills, vast lava fields, and lava rivers both on the surface and underground ('Sparse settlements … within vast stretches of cooled volcanic rock'). Heights and distances below are my estimates from the frames, not canon numbers.

**The city's footing:**
- The city is cut into a plateau of black ropy lava rock, with ridges and tongues roughly 3-10 m high.
- In S1 and S2 the streets are sunken trenches with domes at rock-top level.
- The landing ground just outside the arch is flat: black gravel and ash in S1/S2, pale grey paving in S3.

**Lava flows against ash plains:** the S3 aerial (Pirate siege) shows lobes of black lava pushing into a flat, pale grey-beige ash plain, and the landing field sits on the pale part. The Tribe's camp is also on a pale ash flat ringed by dark ridges about 30-80 m high.

**Mountains and peaks:**
- **The volcano behind the S3 city (Landing Yard MandoS3).** One big conical volcanic peak dominates, roughly 1.5-3 km behind the city and about 500-900 m above it. Its rough rocky flanks have dark streaks and are softened to blue-grey by haze. A darker hill with a building on top looms over the S3 streets (Showdown on Nevarro).
- **The S2 range (NevarroCity-TMCh12).** A continuous wall of steep, eroded grey-blue mountains a few km behind the field of domes. Ridges are layered and get bluer and paler with distance, steam rises at their feet, and the skyline climbs to about a third of the frame height.
- **From the hills above town (Scouts-Waiting).** The town sits in a broad valley floor. Across it are escarpments and flat-topped ridges with cliff faces, about 3-6 km off, with fumaroles steaming.
- **On the lava flats and at the S1 landing site.** Only low, rounded or butte-like dark hills, about 50-200 m high and 1-3 km away. The horizon is low and the sky takes up most of the frame.

**Lava:**
- The lava fields are flat black pahoehoe with branching glowing orange cracks and small channels, plus smoking vents.
- The underground Charon River runs from the city sewers through a ribbed vaulted tunnel and leaves through a round rock portal onto the lava flats.
- Ferry droids pole keelboats on the lava rivers.

**Canyons:**
- The Imperial base hangs on a cliff, about 50-100 m of broken dark rock, above a deep canyon or ravine. A narrow slot canyon with near-vertical walls runs from it.
- Named canyons: Bulloch Canyon (the eastern edge of the Mandalorians' land, from the 'western lava flats' to the canyon) and the 'Black lava canyons' (Ch17).
- Hot springs and geothermal springs are listed but not shown.

**Vegetation:**
- S1/S2: almost none (scattered dry grass tufts).
- S3: planted trees and potted plants in the city, and moss and grass tufts around the homestead pond.

**For the current config:** the existing distant 480 m range fits the S2 look. What it lacks compared with canon:
- a single close conical volcano right behind the town
- escarpments or butte edges and steam plumes at the foot of the mountains
- the strong black-lava against pale-ash ground split
- glowing lava cracks and channels on the flats
- a cliff canyon for the base
canon.palette:
These are measured mean or percentile colours from the stills; the sunset tones are judged by eye.

**Sky (S1/S2):**
- Mostly overcast, cool steel-blue: zenith about #7f91aa, horizon #a9b5c1 to #bcc9d3. The bright cloud break in Ch12 reaches about #e6ebec.
- At dusk the hills read #3d4b62 under a #a6b7cc sky.
- The Ch8 sunset is lavender-pink fading to gold haze.
- S3 is sunnier: pale blue sky with white cumulus.
- From orbit the planet is blue-grey and white.

**Ground and rock:**
- Far mountains through haze: #586670 to #5d7281 (blue-grey).
- Lava rock: blue-black, #1b1f21 / #1e2632 / #171a1a.
- Ash ground: #5d5d5b.
- Pale ash plain: warm grey-beige, #797669 to #847c71.
- S3 paved apron: #aea89f.
- Base cliff: #5c6a6d.

**Buildings:**
- S1/S2 plaster: grey with a faint green cast, stained. Shade #2b3433, mid #5d5c58, sunlit #99a099. Domes are a darker blue-grey, about #3a4547 to #596a74 lit.
- S3 white plaster and towers: mid #9c9d9f, lit #c9c7c8, with cream to orange-banded tops.
- Imperial base hull: cold blue-grey, mid #1f3037, lit #5f7078.

**Lava:**
- Crust and edge: #a11f05 / #a33734.
- Flowing: #d63800.
- Hottest: #f19d23 to #ff8a33.

**Accents:** tan, orange and red cloth awnings and S3 orange and yellow banners. Green appears only in S3 (trees and potted plants) and around the homestead (moss and grass).

**Fog and haze:** blue-grey (not brown), around #9ca6b0 to #a9b5c1, with white steam plumes. The site's existing sky, fog and ground colours already sit inside these ranges.

designs.title: Nevarro, terrain first: a town sunk into black rock below a volcano, with a lava river through it
designs.pitch:
I rebuilt Nevarro starting from the land, using only layer types and props that already exist. No repo files were edited and nothing was committed (git status is clean). All my work is in the git-ignored folder lab/nevarro/tf/.

The land, as measured on the real terrain code:
- A single volcano, about 393 m high, stands right behind the town as you look from the landing. It sits 25° above the horizon at 690 m, and only about 21% of it is fogged.
- A close mountain ring starts at the edge of the walkable area. From the landing the skyline is at least 10° high in all 12 directions I checked.
- A 9 m black lava tableland holds Nevarro City. The city is cut into it as the show's miniature has it (File:NevarroModel.jpg): a sunken square with 9 to 10 m rock walls, three trench streets, and domes and towers standing on the rock at roof height.
- The Charon River comes out of a gorge in the tableland, passes under a crust bridge and runs about 300 m south-east into a sunken lava field, which is about 40% lava. A second arm falls off a vent at the volcano's foot.
- The Imperial base hangs on a 30 m escarpment cliff over a lava channel. A ramp road climbs to it, and a slot canyon (Trexler's run) leads up to a TIE park on top.
- There is also a black western butte with a field of 9 rock spires (the Fingers) in front of it, black ridges to the south, an old lava dome to the north, and a pale ash plain between them all, with black lava lobes and gullies across it.

Measured results:
- **Height:** the walkable area now runs from -1.9 to 263.6 m (it was -3 to 13 m). 1,806 of its 5 m cells are too steep to walk, so cliffs act as natural walls.
- **Lava:** 3.7% of the walkable disc is lava.
- **Reach:** a walk check from the landing reaches every place and every quest spot without wading, apart from the river's own cells. No spot traps the player. This holds on both the high-quality and the small grid.
- **Tests:** every rule in sites.test.js passes, as long as the 8 new Meshy kinds are added to the catalog.
- **Quests:** no quest coordinate has to move.

Files in lab/nevarro/tf/:
- design.mjs: the terrain, ready to paste into outer.js, with its helpers.
- nevarro.site.mjs: the whole site entry, with every thing placed.
- validate.mjs: runs the sites.test.js rules, checks each thing's footing and estimates draw calls and triangles. It also draws the maps.
- probe.mjs: heights, the walk check and the skyline from four spots. spots.mjs, basin.mjs and cost.mjs are smaller helper probes.
- Maps: final.png, final-town.png, final-base.png and town-small.png.
- crops/: the proposed Meshy crops (a1.png and a2.png show them side by side).

All of these run with `node --import ./lab/nevarro/loader.mjs lab/nevarro/tf/<file>`.
designs.terrain:
Copy this into outer.js; design.mjs has it as code.

**Helpers to add to outer.js**
- r1(v) = Math.round(v*10)/10
- along(pts, step): points every `step` metres along a polyline, ends included.
- ramp(a, b, h0, h1, n=12, r=8): copy core.js's ramp (n+1 flats {at, r, edge: r, h} stepping from h0 to h1).
- trench(pts, r, f0, f1=f0, step=6): along(pts, step).map((at, i) => ({ at, r, floor: f0 + (f1 - f0) * i / (len - 1) })). These are pits dug down to an absolute floor.
- river(pts, r, edge=9, step=7): along(pts, step).map(at => ({ at, r, edge, h: BED })). These are flats down to the river bed. Their banks ease out gently, so a player who steps in can walk back out.

**Constants**
- LAVA = 1.5 (lava level); BED = 0.2 (river bed, so lava is 1.3 m deep: waist-deep if you wade).
- FLOOR = 9 (the town floor, its streets, the yard, the landing and the Razor Crest pad).
- TOWN = [140,-90] (unchanged); MESA = [150,-98] (tableland centre); GATE = [58,-37].
- ESC = [-454,278] (escarpment centre); CONE = [660,-380] (volcano).

**ground**
- detail 'ash', detailLook {color 0.75, normal 0.85}, seed 21 (kept), base 5, wind 0.6.

**ground.layers, in this order** (seeds are seed + index×101, so the order matters):
- 0: swell, scale 420, height 4
- 1: hills, scale 130, height 4
- 2: ridges, scale 44, height 2.2 (ropy crust)
- 3: channels, scale 210, depth 3, width 0.05. On the plain these are dry gullies about 3 m deep; in the lava field basin they fill with lava.
- 4: mountains, from 560, to 1150, height 440, scale 620. This is the close ring: about 2 m at r 590, 51–171 m at 800 m, and 126–440 m at 1.15 km.
- 5: island at CONE, r 460, height 300, core 0.1, ragged 0.22 (the volcano). Summit 393 m at [732,-412]. Its flank inside the reach climbs to about 260 m and can be walked up.
- 6: island at CONE, r 70, height -50, core 0.35, ragged 0.2 (the crater; floor at 306.8).
- 7: island at MESA, r 112, height 9, core 0.8, ragged 0.18 (the tableland; top 17.5–19.3 m).
- 8: island at ESC, r 250, height 56, core 0.82, ragged 0.22 (the escarpment; top about 62–63 m; its NE face is a cliff).
- 9: island at [340,280], r 250, height -6.5, core 0.45, ragged 0.3 (the sag under the lava field).
- 10: island at [150,250], r 120, height 34, core 0.2, ragged 0.4 (black ridge to the south).
- 11: island at [70,330], r 110, height 28, core 0.2, ragged 0.4 (black ridge to the south).
- 12: island at [-420,-180], r 120, height 42, core 0.78, ragged 0.18 (the western butte; top about 51 m).
- 13: island at [-120,-430], r 120, height 32, core 0.45, ragged 0.3 (the old lava dome to the north).

**ground.flats, in this order** (the landing and place flats are appended after them by siteOf):
- The base's lava channel: river([[-300,58],[-270,82],[-240,106],[-214,140]], 5, 12, 6).
- The base road: ramp([-160,206], [-226,176], 8, 33, 10, 6). It rises 25 m over 72 m (walkable slope, normal 0.945) and passes round the channel's end.
- The Charon River, in two runs with a crust bridge between them (the gap from [250,124] to [260,152] is the dry crossing):
  - river([[178,14],[194,56],[226,98],[250,124]], 6)
  - river([[260,152],[272,176],[300,214],[322,252]], 6)
- The volcano arm: river([[430,-60],[420,20],[380,90],[352,150],[332,212]], 5, 8).

**ground.pits** (dug after the flats)
- Main street: trench([[104,-67],[58,-37]], 9, 9).
- North lane: trench([[106,-117],[62,-152]], 8, 9).
- Back lane: trench([[158,-52],[166,-30]], 7, 9). It stops about 12 m short of the gorge.
- River gorge: trench([[172,-10],[178,14]], 8, 0.2, 0.2, 5). It cuts the tableland's south cliff; the gorge head wall is at z ≈ -18 and the rim at about 20 m.
- Trexler's slot canyon: trench([[-286,176],[-318,214],[-342,262]], 7, 33, 62, 5). It rises from the base floor at 33 m and comes out on top of the escarpment at 61.2 m.

**Place flats** (on each place)
- town {r 44, edge 6, h 9}: the bowl. The walls are steep enough to block walking.
- yard {r 30, edge 14, h 9}
- crest {r 30, h 9}
- base {r 38, edge 6, h 33}: the terrace notch in the cliff.
- lava {r 9, edge 10, h 2.9}: a crust floor.
- bluff {r 14} (comes out at 71.7 m).
- homestead {r 14} (comes out at about 9.8 m).
- land: { at: [0,0], yaw: 0.6, h: 9 }. The landing test grid gives normal 1.000 and h 9.0, which is above the lava.

**water**
- { level: 1.5, color: '#ff4a0e', deep: '#2a0904', kind: 'lava', glow: 1.7 }

**fog, sky and light**
- fog: { color: '#9aa6b2', density: 0.0007 }. Share fogged: 12% at 500 m, 39% at 1 km, 67% at 1.5 km.
- sky: sky('#5d7190', '#aab6c4', '#ffe2c0', { clouds: { cover: 0.6, color: '#c9ced4', shade: '#4c5058', scale: 0.6, speed: 0.006 } })
- light: { sun: 2.3, sky: '#b0bccd', ground: '#2f2e33', ambient: 0.66 }. This is a little cooler and darker than now, to balance the orange light the lava adds from below (0.9).

**palette** (pale ash low, black lava high, a warm black crust near the lava)
- low '#6f6b62', high '#24272c', rock '#15181b', accent '#22262b', deep '#1b1d20', mark '#18191c'
- hLow 10.5, hHigh 16, rockAt 0.36, accentCover 0.3 (black lava lobes across the pale plain), grain 0.6, roughness 0.9
- ripple { strength 0.02, scale 3, wind 0.5 }
- wet { level 1.5, band 5, color '#2a1612' }. This band darkens the low lava-field crust and the river banks, which the height colour alone would paint pale.

**weather**
- [{ kind: 'ash', count: 700, color: '#5d5f66' }, { kind: 'embers', count: 160 }]

**Other site fields**
- dust '#3a3a3e'; edge: 'Nothing out there but more rock and the mountains. Turn back.'

**Skyline from the landing** (highest angle, distance, share fogged)
- 0°: 10.0° at 1650 m (fog 0.74)
- 60°: 17.6° at 1155 m (fog 0.48)
- 90°: 13.6°
- 210°: 16.2°
- 270°: 16.8°
- 330°, the volcano behind the town: 24.9° at 690 m (fog 0.21)

From the town, the rock walls fill 120–180° and the volcano is 31.6° high at 480 m. From the base terrace, the cliff behind runs from 90° to 210° at about 30°, and the view in front is open.

designs.risks:
**1. Lava light.** Lava adds a scene-wide HemisphereLight('#000', '#ff6a1a', 0.9) and lava sound. I lowered the light (sun 2.3, ground #2f2e33, ambient 0.66) to keep the steel-blue look, but it needs a check in the browser. If it still reads warm, drop ambient to about 0.6.

**2. Lava doesn't hurt.** River beds are 1.3 m below the surface, so a player who wades in is waist-deep and the river looks like a hot ford. Flat-built banks (edge 9–12) let them climb back out; the walk check found 0 trap cells on both grids. The basin has 110 cells deeper than 1.6 m, where a player can go under the plane.

**3. Small tier (8 m cells).** The bowl reads as an octagon and the 14–18 m trench streets soften into ditches. Reach still checks out. Things placed with abs y 9 in the main street (2 house fronts) may sink a little; stalls and lamps follow the ground on purpose.

**4. Scatter ignores trenches and rivers.** The clear values (18–22 m around place flats) keep big rocks and spires out of the bowl, the main street and the yard. A few small rocks and lavacracks may still land in the lanes or under the lava (harmless).

**5. Meshy lifts from busy stills:**
- Karga stands in front of the tower; droids stand on the keelboat; a trooper is beside the house front; the portal is shot from inside the tunnel.
- Use each lane's `yaw` to make the models face +z, and judge each one on its sheet before fetching.
- charonportal may need the 36-credit prompt route instead.
- nevarrobase needs hero: true and lod (30k triangles, 2K maps) and must stay under 4 MB.

**6. Fitting the base.** nevarrobase is 52 m long, placed at rel [-22.2,13.5] yaw 2.1 against a curved cut wall. Its ends may poke into the rock; adjust them in the browser. The pad hangs about 10 m out over the 33 m drop on a floor disc. Bespin and Mustafar already use floor discs this way, but it needs checking in the browser.

**7. Flyovers.** Flights are straight 3.2 km lines at alt + ground near the player. At alt 150 a pass can still clip the top of the volcano, and far passes clip the mountain ring, as on other worlds.

**8. Budget baseline.** The +10% rule against today's Nevarro (87 calls, 0.94M triangles) cannot hold for this. It fits the absolute caps (see the budget estimate). The owner must agree to the absolute caps or to a new baseline.

**9. Re-rolled layout.** A new layer list and scatter order re-roll all noise and scatter. Every old Nevarro screenshot or baseline becomes invalid. The seed (21) is kept.

**10. Volcano detail.** The summit (393 m at [732,-412]) and crater sit on the coarse far grid (cells about 30–40 m), so the crater rim is blocky. The plumes cover it.

**11. Tests.** sites.test.js will fail until the 8 new kinds have catalog entries (catalog/outer.js, made: 'meshy', hero/lod for nevarrobase), committed GLBs and a line in public/cc0/README.md. The lane is either a new scripts/meshy-galaxy-buildings-nevarro.mjs plus its -tasks.json and one Object.assign line, or entries added to the back lane.

**12. Canon mixing.** S1/S2 trench streets and domes stand next to S3 towers and the statue. This is deliberate (New Republic era) but mixes seasons.

**13. Garrison.** The holder's troopers patrol 26–48 m round [0,0]. The X-wings and cargo are kept outside that loop, but the yard is busy.
designs.budgetEstimate:
**Draw calls:** about 238 for things and scatter, from validate.mjs using measured costs (each Meshy model is 1 draw; parked ships 5, lamps 2, speederbike 13, eweb 4). Adding terrain, sky, lava, weather and about 30 actors gives roughly 290–320 at worst, under the 600 cap.

**Triangles:** about 0.70M in things (16 house fronts at 10k is 160k, 12 rim domes and towers 144k, base 30k with lod, cantina 20k, razorcrest 30k) and about 0.38M in scatter (100 lavarocks are 300k of that). With the terrain grid and actors, the total is about 1.4–1.5M, under 2.5M. Cutting the lavarock scatter from 100 to 60 saves about 120k if needed.

**Models:**
- Nevarro's own GLBs now: about 6.9 MB.
- Existing models brought in: about 2.8 MB (lambda, turret, eweb, welderrack, ammocan, speedertruck, swoop, vaporator, speederbike, scouttrooper).
- New Meshy models: about 6.2 MB (base about 3 MB plus a lod of about 0.7 MB; the other seven about 0.3–0.4 MB each).
- Total: about 16 MB for Nevarro's own models, or about 19–20 MB fetched including the player's ship and shared files. Well under 40 MB.

**Meshy credits:** 8 lifts at 33 each is 264. With charonportal on the prompt route it is 267. With about 70 kept for two re-dos it stays at or under about 340, well under the 500 budget. Dropping the keelboat saves 33.

**Load and fill:**
- The walkable area goes from -3…13 m to -1.9…263.6 m, with 1,806 too-steep cells.
- Lava covers 3.7% of the walkable disc (1,627 cells) and about 40% of the lava-field basin.
- The ground has 14 layers, 128 flats and 55 pits; the high-quality grid builds in about 3 s in Node.

designs.title: Nevarro rebuild, landmark-first: Nevarro City sunk in its lava shelf, the cliff-top Imperial base, the Charon River
designs.pitch:
I didn't edit or commit any repo files. The whole design is written as a candidate site entry in the git-ignored scratch file /home/user/new-portfolio-website/lab/nevarro/landmark/nevarro.mjs. It uses outer.js's own idioms, so it can be pasted in nearly as written.

I probed it against the real terrain.js and siteOf with lab/nevarro/landmark/probe.mjs. The probe checks the same things the tests check, plus walking routes, building overlaps and the scatter (replayed with the scene's own rng). It writes a full dump of the placed spots to site.json. The pictures are map.png (whole world), town.png (town zoom) and view-*.png (rough perspective renders). Everything below has been measured against the real terrain code.

**The idea:** build Nevarro City the way the show's effects artists built it (File:NevarroModel.jpg). The town is sunk into a shelf of black lava rock.
- The town floor is a bowl 152 m across at a height of 11 m.
- The rock round it is a natural wall 6 to 11 m high. Stepped stone domes sit along its top at rock level, as in the S2 shot of the domes over the black rock.
- Inside are dense plaster streets:
  - an outer ring of 18 buildings with their backs to the rock;
  - an inner ring of 12;
  - a paved market square in front of Greef's cantina;
  - the Magistrate's hall on the square's east side;
  - the IG-11 statue by the cantina door.
- Three ways out are cut through the rock:
  - the West Gate (the S2 arch), facing the landing yard where an X-wing is parked. It is 58 m from where you step out.
  - the South Gate, toward the lava river and the lava flats.
  - the North Lane (a new S1 tall arch), out to the Razor Crest.
- Inside the West Gate's cut, two great pillars hold a footbridge over Gate Street (the S1 inner gate).
- Behind the cantina, the covert's way down is a funnel in the street. At its foot is the lava that runs under the city, the sewer mouth and the Armorer.
- The Charon River comes out of a tunnel mouth in the town's south-east rock. It runs in a 15 to 20 m lava gorge, under a rock bridge (a second tunnel mouth on its far side), and out into the lava flats: black crust 1 to 2 m above a lobed lava pool.
- The Imperial base is the canon cliff fortress: a 100 m Meshy model lifted from the only exterior still. It is built into the 33 m lip of a lava canyon cut in a 26 m plateau, its pad hanging over the lava, with TIEs, barracks, a watchtower and a mast on the plateau top.
- Behind the town, from the landing, there is a 57 m watch hill with an S3 white tower on top. Behind that is a 660 m volcano 1.14 km out, and the mountain ring now starts at 540 m.

Fog drops from 0.0012 to 0.00085, so all of it reads.

**Quests:** no quest coordinate changes. The town place's centre moves, but the cantina is placed so it sits at exactly [140,-90] with yaw 0.3 (checked), so the zone door [143,-80.4] and back [143.7,-78] don't move. Every other quest spot is untouched.

**Spend:** about 339 Meshy credits for 10 new kinds (375 with an optional Nevarro cantina), leaving about 100 for re-lifts.
designs.terrain:
Everything below is in the `nevarro.ground` / `water` of lab/nevarro/landmark/nevarro.mjs.

**Basics:** seed 21 (kept), detail 'ash', detailLook as now.

**Layers, in this order.** Indices 0-2 are the old ones, so their noise seeds don't move. The new layers are appended.
- **0** swell, scale 380, height 10 (unchanged).
- **1** hills, scale 120, height 10 (was 8).
- **2** mountains, from 540, to 1900, height 520, scale 900 (was 650/3000/480/1100). It reaches about 157 m at r 700, 439 at r 900 and 641 at r 1200, and adds nothing inside REACH.
- **3** island at [148.8,-65.4], r 120, height 10, core 0.75, ragged 0.18. This is the town's lava shelf. Its rim reads 17-22 m at r 87.
- **4** island at [-300,205], r 200, height 26, core 0.72, ragged 0.15. This is the base plateau. Its top is 30.5 m and its flanks are walkable (normal 0.78 or more).
- **5** island at [283.8,-217.8], r 100, height 50, core 0.28, ragged 0.2. This is the watch hill. Its top is 57 m, and it can be climbed from the North Lane side (normal 0.70).
- **6** island at [700,-900], r 620, height 480, core 0.1, ragged 0.2. This is the volcano. Its drawn top is about 660 m, 1.14 km from the landing and about 61% fogged.
- **7** island at [325,245], r 150, height -9, core 0.5, ragged 0.4. This is the lava-flats basin. The crust sits at -1 to -3 m round a lobed lava pool of about 140×100 m. This is sensitive: -7.5 leaves only a small pool.

I dropped the extra ridges layers I tried, because they cost 33 ms each.

**Lava.** `water: { level: -3, color: '#ff4a0a', deep: '#2a0904', kind: 'lava', glow: 1.8 }`. Undug ground in the walkable disc never goes below -1.1, so lava shows only where it is dug and in the basin. The 'Lava' line gives the area under lava as 2.2 ha.

**Code that must ship with the assets:**

2. Add the 10 (or 11) kinds to the back lane's line in public/cc0/README.md (line 28), plus `nevarrobase.lod1.glb`.
3. The lane entries go in scripts/meshy-galaxy-buildings-back.mjs, with tasks in -back-tasks.json. Run lift (or images), then sheet, review, then models, then fetch, then sheet.
4. Arch solids:

For example: `PROPS.nevarroarch = (k) => ({ object: k.build([]), solids: [{ circle: [-4.4,0,1.1] }, { circle: [4.4,0,1.1] }] })`.

designs.risks:
**1. The lava's light.** Lava water adds a fixed HemisphereLight('#000','#ff6a1a',0.9) from below (water.js:123). It will warm the cool steel-blue town's undersides.
- I lowered ambient to 0.64 and light.ground to '#2e3036' to compensate.
- If it still reads orange, the only fix is a one-line engine knob (`w.light ?? 0.9`), which is not in the engine map.

**2. Terrain build time.** It is 607 ms on this machine, against Tatooine's 546 ms and old Nevarro's 133 ms. The cost is 28 pits and 19 flats at about 6 ms each, and 5 islands at about 35 ms each.
- Optional, not a feature: in terrain.js's levelled() and dug(), add a square bounding-box reject and use `Math.sqrt(dx*dx+dz*dz)` in place of `Math.hypot`. I tested this on a copy (lab/nevarro/landmark/terrain-fast.mjs): heights are identical, this Nevarro drops to 348 ms and Tatooine to 210 ms.
- Without it, don't add more pits or flats; use fewer gates first.

**3. Budget baseline.** Against today's numbers (87 calls, 939k triangles), the `+10%` rule would cap the world at about 96 calls. This design needs the owner to accept the absolute caps instead.

**4. Meshy lifts.**
- The tower's frame is half-blocked by Karga, so its lift has to invent the base.
- The base is a very wide crop, and its depth will be guessed. After fetch, measure it and reset its y and offset (roof 2-4 m above 30.5, back at least 4 m behind the lip at s 46).
- Keep about 100 credits spare for re-lifts (3 each) and one model remake (30).

**5. Cantina door.** The cantina's world spot must stay at [140,-90] yaw 0.3. The town frame computes it from local [2,-26.05] yaw -0.12 (checked to 0.01 m). If anyone moves the town, recompute: door = cantina + turn([3,9.6], 0.3 - 0) in world terms, and back the same way.

**6. Grid resolution.** The ground grid is 5 m, and 8 m on the small tier.
- The bowl wall (5 m edge), the 12-16 m cuts and the 7.5 m covert pool soften on the small tier. The North Lane is the narrowest at 12 m.
- The volcano's summit is about 50 m between grid lines, so it is soft-topped.

**7. Steep-sided traps.**
- The river's upper stretch is closed by the portal and the bridge, and the canyon is closed at both ends. Each has an exit cone, and both were walked out by the probe.
- The covert pool is guarded by the rock's r 8.2 solid.
- Verify in-engine with real collision. The probe ignores solids and the jump.

**8. The lava basin is sensitive.** At height -9 there is a lobed pool of about 140×100 m; at -7.5 only a small pool. The crust sits within about 1 m of the lava plane, so its edges will shimmer.

**9. Scatter is replayed with the same rng and order.** Any reorder reshuffles it. About 20 items land in lava (rocks standing in lava, which is fine) and 1 lavarock lands in a cut.

**10. Content.**
- IG-11's roaming actor is removed, since he is now the statue (S2-S3). The era mixes S1 Greef lines with S3 towers, which is deliberate: the old town plus Karga's new quarter.
- Nothing is sequel-trilogy. Prompts never name the films.

**11. Garrison.** Things in the yard were moved off the garrison beats (bevelcrates moved to [52,-10], [38,30], [-30,36]). The X-wing at [24,-46] is 15 m clear of the 48 m diamond.

**12. Hills layer change.** It went from 8 to 10, which raises or lowers the crest and protect area by about 2 m (Mando now at 8.4). The crest flat covers it, and the protect route is clear (normal 1.0).

**13. Paving.** The `deck` square floor is 0.3 m up, so things on it carry y 0.3. Life uses floors.

**14. Some routes are not walkable, by design.**
- The rim top is cut by the three ways out.
- From the South Gate you can't go straight east to the hill (the gorge head is in the way). Use the North Lane or walk over the rim.

designs.title: Nevarro, player-first: land at the gate, then loop the valley
designs.pitch:
You land on black gravel about 70 m from the city gate, already facing it. Behind the arch you see domes and aerials on a black lava-rock shelf, and a hazy volcano rises 12° up, just behind the town. Turn round and the Imperial base sits on a 34 m cliff across the valley, with a red beacon and smoke. A five-minute walk then loops the valley clockwise, with something new every 60–150 m. Each district looks different:

1. **Landing yard** (marker blocks, Dengar's Punishing One, hunters, a speeder bike).
2. **Gate and bazaar.** A 29 m-wide street cut 7 m down into the rock, lined with shopfronts and orange-awning stalls. A concrete bridge crosses it and a happabore blocks it.
3. **The square.** Gideon's TIE stands on the dirt and Greef's cantina sits opposite the gate. Greef gives the puck quest here.
4. **Optional side trips:**
   - a 10° ramp up to **the rooftops** (domes, aerials, a view over everything);
   - **the covert**, a sunken forge yard whose smoke column shows from the landing.
5. **Back street** past the Client's safe house, out to **the Charon's mouth**, where a glowing lava stream runs out of a rock tunnel.
6. **Lava flats** (cracks, lava spouts, vents, blurrgs), then **Mando's camp** by the stream for the protect quest. Kuiil, Cara and Grogu are there.
7. **The scouts' rise.** Two comic scout troopers and a speeder bike.
8. **The black canyon.** A 30 m-deep slot with a crashed TIE, climbing up behind the base.
9. **The Imperial base.** The puck objective, on a bastion over the cliff. It gives the best view of the valley: town, smoke, lava cracks and the volcano in one frame.
10. **The Imperial road**, a 17° lamp-lit ramp, straight back down to the yard. From there the cantina is 180 m away to hand in the puck, and the Armorer's new beskar quest is next door.

The intended loop is about 1.7 m... measured at 1,704 m. That is about 3.8 minutes running or 8.6 minutes walking, and less with the speeder bikes. Every leg was checked for walkable slope (no step over 33°) and for clear passage past every building footprint.

**Files** (all scratch, in the git-ignored /home/user/new-portfolio-website/lab/nevarro/player/; no repo file was touched):
- **site.mjs** is the whole entry, ready to paste: data plus the small helpers `line`, `ramp`, `turn`, `facing`, `townAt` and `baseAt`.
- **validate.mjs** runs the sites.test rules, footing, overlaps, the walk, the landing view and the cost.
- **shots/*.png** are renders from a scratch app copy on port 5197, with stand-ins for the new models.
- **map.png** and **town.png** are the overview maps.

This is the most faithful Nevarro. The town is sunk into a lava-rock shelf, as the show's miniature has it. The base sits on a 33 m canyon lip, which matches the canon text in lab/nevarro/text/Nevarro_Imperial_base.txt: 'built into the side of a cliff overlooking a canyon'. The Charon River comes out of tunnel mouths, and the IG-11 statue is by the cantina door, which is the canon spot near the school entrance.

What my probe confirmed (lab/nevarro/judge/judge.mjs, using the real terrain.js and siteOf):
- The cantina ends up at exactly [140.00,-90.00] with yaw 0.300, so the cantina zone is untouched. Its door and back both stand on flat ground at 11.0 m.
- Every quest spot is flat (normal 1.00) on both grid tiers.
- Terrain build is 676 ms on the high tier and 241 ms on the small tier, against 126 ms today.
- The walkable area runs from -11.2 to 69.7 m, with 307 too-steep cells. 2.0% of it is lava.

Canon slip: the Armorer and two living Tribe Mandalorians stand in the covert in the same world as the IG-11 statue. The statue only exists after Chapter 8, when the Tribe was massacred and the covert abandoned.

It isn't a site-only change:
- PROPS stand-ins in props/outer.js for the arch solids;
- an optional terrain.js speedup.

Costs and risks:
- It needs 10 or 11 Meshy assets. The riskiest is the 100 m hero base lifted from one wide still, at 30k triangles on a 2K texture, and players stand 34 m from it.
- Worst-case credits are about 475 of the roughly 500 cap.
- Draw-call figures (at most about 370) are estimates, not measured.
- In its own box render from the landing, the town hides behind its rim, so the domes and towers on the rim have to carry the view.

It has the best play design. You land facing the gate, and a 1.7 km loop has something new every 60 to 150 m. The about-texts point to the next stop. It adds a new 'forge' quest (a use step after the puck), place crew lines and two speeder bikes. It is the only proposal checked in the real app (shots/*.png, with stand-in models).
